_note: Starting point for the state claims-handling compliance matrix. Each loaded rule was checked against the cited text on the date in 'verified' (see 'verified_url'); rules change, so Compliance must still confirm each launch state before go-live. States not listed fall back to the NAIC model as a placeholder only.

default.source: NAIC Unfair Property/Casualty Claims Settlement Practices Model Regulation (MDL-902)
default.decision_trigger: after proof of loss is received
default.extension_rule: If more time is needed, notify the claimant within 21 days with the reasons, then every 45 days until decided (model rule; the state's own rule governs).
default.denial_notice: [TBD — Compliance: this state's required denial / complaint notice] The NAIC model requires a written denial citing the specific policy provision, condition or exclusion relied on.

CA.source: California Fair Claims Settlement Practices Regulations
CA.decision_trigger: after proof of claim is received
CA.extension_rule: If more time is needed, give written notice within 40 days stating what additional information is needed and why, then every 30 calendar days until a determination is made or notice of legal action is served.
CA.denial_notice: If you believe all or part of this claim has been wrongfully denied or rejected, you may have the matter reviewed by the California Department of Insurance, Consumer Communications Bureau, [TBD — Compliance: current mailing address of the CDI unit that reviews claims practices], telephone 1-800-927-4357.

TX.source: Texas Insurance Code, Chapter 542, Subchapter B (Prompt Payment of Claims)
TX.decision_trigger: after all items, statements and forms requested are received
TX.extension_rule: If the insurer cannot accept or reject within the period, notify the claimant within it, stating the reasons more time is needed, then accept or reject within 45 days of that notice. Eligible surplus lines insurers have 30 business days to acknowledge and 20 business days to pay.
TX.denial_notice: This notice states the reasons we are rejecting your claim: [reasons]. [TBD — Compliance: Texas Department of Insurance complaint notice wording and contact details]

NY.source: New York Insurance Regulation 64 (Unfair Claims Settlement Practices)
NY.decision_trigger: after a properly executed proof of loss is received
NY.extension_rule: If more time is needed, notify the claimant in writing within 15 business days of the proof of loss, then every 90 days with the reasons more time is needed. Payment is due 5 business days after receipt of the settlement agreement or performance of its conditions, whichever is later.
NY.denial_notice: A rejection is given in writing, explains the specific reasons for disclaiming coverage, and states any policy provision limiting your right to sue us: [policy provision]. [TBD — Compliance: NY DFS complaint notice wording]

FL.decision_trigger: after notice of the claim is received (pay or deny)
FL.extension_rule: Begin investigation within 7 days of proof-of-loss statements and complete any physical inspection within 30 days. The 60-day pay-or-deny deadline applies unless failure is caused by factors beyond the insurer's control; late payments bear interest at the s. 55.03 rate.
FL.denial_notice: We are giving you a reasonable explanation in writing of the basis in the policy, in relation to the facts or applicable law, for this denial or partial denial: [explanation]. [TBD — Compliance: Florida Department of Financial Services consumer contact wording]

IL.source: Illinois Administrative Code, Title 50, Part 919 (Improper Claims Practices)
IL.decision_trigger: within a reasonable time (no fixed day count in Part 919)
IL.extension_rule: Communicate with all insureds and claimants within 21 working days after notification of loss when liability is reasonably clear. A denial or lower offer needs a reasonable written explanation within 30 days, setting out the policy definition, limitation, exclusion or condition relied on, accompanied by the Notice of Availability of the Department of Insurance. Payment is offered within 30 days after liability is affirmed.
IL.denial_notice: Part 919 of the Rules of the Illinois Department of Insurance requires that our company advise you that, if you wish to take this matter up with the Illinois Department of Insurance, it maintains a Consumer Division in Chicago at 115 S. LaSalle Street, 13th Floor, Chicago, Illinois 60603 and in Springfield at 320 West Washington Street, Springfield, Illinois 62767.

OH.source: Ohio Administrative Code 3901-1-54 (Unfair property/casualty claims settlement practices)
OH.decision_trigger: after properly executed proof(s) of loss are received
OH.extension_rule: If more time is needed, notify the claimant within the 21 days with the reasons, then send written status at least every 45 days. Deadlines falling on a weekend or holiday move to the next business day.
OH.denial_notice: A denial on the grounds of a specific policy provision, condition or exclusion must refer to that provision: [policy provision]. [TBD — Compliance: Ohio Department of Insurance consumer contact wording]

PA.source: Pennsylvania Code, Title 31, Chapter 146 (Unfair Claims Settlement Practices)
PA.decision_trigger: after properly executed proofs of loss are received
PA.extension_rule: If the investigation remains incomplete, send the claimant a letter with the reasons more time is needed 30 days from the initial notification and every 45 days after. The Department's inquiries are answered within 15 working days.
PA.denial_notice: The denial is given in writing and refers to the provision, condition or exclusion relied on: [policy provision]. [TBD — Compliance: Pennsylvania Insurance Department consumer contact wording]

GA.source: Georgia Comp. R. & Regs. 120-2-52-.03 (first-party property damage claims) and O.C.G.A. §33-6-34
GA.decision_trigger: after completed proof of loss is received (30 days from report if no proof of loss is required)
GA.extension_rule: If more time is needed, notify the claimant within 5 business days after receiving the completed proof of loss; the total time to accept or deny may not exceed 60 days from notice of the claim unless requested information has not been provided.
GA.denial_notice: A denial is given in writing with a reasonable and accurate explanation of its basis: [explanation]. [TBD — Compliance: Georgia Office of Commissioner of Insurance consumer contact wording]
GA.verification_note: Checked against a law-firm summary quoting the regulation; confirm against the official Georgia rule text.

MI.source: Michigan Insurance Code MCL 500.2006 (timely payment of claims)
MI.decision_trigger: no fixed decision deadline; payment timing below
MI.extension_rule: Specify in writing the materials that make up a satisfactory proof of loss within 30 days of receiving the claim, unless it is settled within 30 days. Benefits not paid within 60 days after satisfactory proof of loss bear 12% simple interest per year from that date.
MI.denial_notice: [TBD — Compliance: Michigan DIFS denial and complaint notice wording]
MI.verification_note: Official page blocks automated access; checked against search excerpts of the official page and attorney summaries. Confirm against the statute text.
